C05-M04-L04-F1.title: Unauthenticated vs authenticated scan: what each can see
C05-M04-L04-F1.caption: The outside and inside views of the same host are complementary: one guesses patch level from labels, the other reads it directly.
C05-M04-L04-F1.alt: Two columns separated by vs. Unauthenticated (outside view): open ports; banners and headers; protocol behaviour; anonymous responses; patch level guessed from labels. Authenticated (inside view): installed package inventory; kernel and OS build; configuration files and registry; non-listening software; patch level read directly.
C05-M04-L04-F1.note: Run both and reconcile: use the inside view to confirm or dismiss outside guesses.

C05-M04-L04-F2.title: One authenticated Linux scan, message by message
C05-M04-L04-F2.caption: The exchange behind an authenticated scan: SSH login, OS and package inventory, facts stored, compared with advisories, result recorded.
C05-M04-L04-F2.alt: Sequence diagram with four lanes: OpenVAS scanner, Lab host (sshd), Knowledge base (Redis), Advisory data (feed). Scanner to host: SSH login with the scan account's key. Host to scanner (reply): login accepted. Scanner to host: read-only commands for OS release and installed packages. Host to scanner (reply): release + package list. Scanner to knowledge base: write facts. Knowledge base to scanner (reply): local checks read the facts back. Scanner to advisory data: look up fixed versions. Advisory data to scanner (reply): fixed version, compared with the installed version to produce a result.

messages.label: SSH login with scan account key

C05-M04-L04-F2.note: If the login fails, nothing after it happens: always check authentication status before trusting a quiet report.
